page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E6.Ax.Flex.1-4 is an entry-level virtual machine instance configured with AMD EPYC 9J45 processors operating at a base frequency of 2.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The server allocates two dedicated virtual CPUs backed by one physical core with two execution threads. System memory is provisioned at 4.0 GB total, yielding a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not bundle integrated local storage or hardware accelerators, requiring external block volumes for persistent operating system and application storage. Network connectivity includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

With a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory allocation ratio, the VM.Standard.E6.Ax.Flex.1-4 prioritizes lean resource consumption suitable for processing tasks with modest working sets. The reliance on remote network-attached storage introduces dependency on block storage latency and bandwidth rather than fast local NVMe disks. Because compute resources are dedicated rather than shared, the server avoids CPU credit constraints and resource contention, though the single physical core caps parallel execution throughput.

From an infrastructure efficiency perspective, the VM.Standard.E6.Ax.Flex.1-4 provides dedicated x86_64 processing at low resource overhead. This setup is best suited for small-scale production or staging tasks that do not justify multi-core or high-memory footprints. Typical applications include microservices, API routing, lightweight web serving, automation scripts, and background development environments.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E6.Ax.Flex.1-4 is a compute-focused flexible virtual machine powered by the x86_64 AMD EPYC 9J45 processor running at 2.7 GHz. The instance delivers two dedicated virtual CPUs mapped across a single physical core with multithreading, paired with 4.0 GB of system RAM at a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Hardware accelerators such as discrete GPUs are absent, and no local disk storage is included, requiring cloud block storage for operating systems and application data. A single complimentary public IPv4 address is provided for external connectivity. Due to its dedicated CPU allocation, the configuration avoids the performance volatility common in burstable virtual cores while offering economical compute sizing. The VM.Standard.E6.Ax.Flex.1-4 is suited for lightweight workloads with modest memory demands, including basic microservices, utility tasks, development environments, and low-traffic web serving.
